newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian troops brace for possible rebel attacks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian troops brace for possible rebel attacks.

text.p: Colombian security forces in Bogota were on alert on Sunday for possible guerrilla strikes after Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra said he was aware of rebel plans to attack parts of the capital.
Esguerra told El Espectador newspaper on Saturday the planned spiral in rebel activity had been uncovered by military intelligence and was expected to take place over the weekend.
The U.S. embassy issued a warning late on Friday to American residents not to leave Bogota because of the risk of rebel actions.

Two guerrillas and two policemen were killed when units of the left-wing Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia overran a police station in Acevedo, in Colombia's central Huila province on Saturday, police sources said on Sunday.
In a separate clash also on Saturday between police and National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas in Segovia, a mining town of northwestern Antioquia province, four civilians were injured.
In the north and northeast, ELN guerrillas burned four passenger buses, police confirmed.

Colombia's guerrillas launched one of their bloodiest offensives in decades at the end of August and at least 120 people, mostly soldiers and police have been killed. Part of their strategy has been to blockade major highways and to burn vehicles which run the gauntlet of the rebel threat.
Last week, national newspapers reported that Colombia had been split in two by the armed blockades and said that at least 15 provinces had so far been affected.
